body:
# [Experiment] E-CURRENT-MOMENT-WP-20261018: current-superbatch weighted-Pearson replay

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Proposal only: no implementation, adapter, clean registry binding, profile, fit, or grade. This is a narrow continuation of H-055; the experiment ID is `E-CURRENT-MOMENT-WP-20261018`. Pinned source: `1d57ed815c18eb278bcdd0207369b200970b28fb`. The receiving run owner is unassigned; the proposal branch is experiment/current-moment-wp-replay. Reuse the canonical GRU factory, but its exact model/input/LR registry entries remain unbound. `training_authorized=false`; `launch_ready=false`. The shared publication registers this continuation and experiment in the append-only ledgers.

2. **Why it should work.** Per-chunk Pearson can be degenerate when a chunk's target is constant; a decayed pooled-moment objective instead mixes statistics from earlier parameter states and does not give those earlier outputs the current objective's exact derivative. The candidate forms the official clipped weighted-Pearson objective over all eligible rows in one fixed 64-complete-sequence superbatch, at one frozen parameter state, then replays the same truncated chunks and applies cached output derivatives before one update. Unlike the separate H-RR17-19 adaptive-TBPTT continuation, this keeps K=500 and every detach boundary fixed; it changes only the objective-gradient estimator. Because the WMSE control shares the same 64-sequence macrostep, this comparison tests the objective conditional on that macrostep, not whether the larger macrostep beats the canonical training schedule. Predicted first evidence is agreement between the analytic output gradient, an autograd/finite-difference oracle, and deterministic replay on small synthetic cases; only then could a matched endpoint comparison test quality. Strong alternatives are that WMSE optimizes this recurrent model better, that macrobatch correlation is too noisy, or that clipped rows carry too little useful gradient. The discriminating control is the same macrostep and row population trained with canonical WMSE; no per-chunk-correlation or EMA arm is proposed.

3. **Compute advantage.** The candidate adds a graphless forward and a replay/backward forward, plus an ephemeral output-gradient buffer, relative to ordinary one-pass WMSE accumulation. Both arms use the same large macrostep and optimizer-update count, so the comparison does not silently change cadence. Cost and memory are unknown until an actual-device profile. A useful future result requires paired WP delta at least `+0.0005` and total candidate fit time no more than `2x` the matched control; these are proposed gates, not measurements or a scaling law. There is no teacher/cache generation or serving-time overhead.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Two arms: (A) label-only canonical WMSE control; (B) current-superbatch `clip2-WP` loss with two-pass output-gradient replay. Each paired fold/seed cell starts from the same cold initialization within the pair; different cells use their own seeds. No teacher, distillation target or warm parent is used; normal sequence-local GRU state is carried across chunks and reset only at sequence boundaries. No target/prediction cache persists across macrosteps. Only the candidate's temporary within-step output-gradient buffer is retained, then discarded.

   Both arms process identical sequence groups and row order: 64 complete 20,000-row sequences per superbatch, with the final partial superbatch included and scored on its actual eligible rows. Both perform one optimizer update per superbatch, for the same six epochs and update count; use the fixed epoch-5 endpoint. Within each sequence, carry recurrent state across K=500-row TBPTT chunks, detach at each chunk boundary, and reset at the sequence boundary. Replay records/restores the detached boundary states and RNG so its second pass matches the graphless pass before the single update. This is exact only for the fixed superbatch and its truncated graph, not for the full training fold or full BPTT, and not an average of per-chunk metrics.

   The candidate clips prediction and target to `[-2,2]`, weights each eligible row by the absolute clipped target, calculates separate weighted Pearson coefficients for the two targets over the current superbatch, then minimizes their negative mean. Its analytical derivative for one head, with `q=clip(p,-2,2)`, `z=clip(y,-2,2)`, weighted means `mu_p, mu_y`, unnormalized centered sums `Spp=sum(w*(q-mu_p)^2)` and `Syy=sum(w*(z-mu_y)^2)`, and coefficient `r`, is `clip'(p) * w * [r*(q-mu_p)/Spp - (z-mu_y)/sqrt(Syy*Spp)]`; multiply by `1/2` for the two-head mean. If centered sums are normalized by `W=sum(w)`, use `w/W`. Match the scorer degeneracy contract: zero contribution when total weight <1e-8 or either weighted standard deviation <=1e-8, and log the count; near-constant stability and the clipping-boundary subgradient convention must pass the no-fit numerical gate before any fit.

   The control is explicitly weighted MSE: the mean of the two heads of sum(w*(raw_prediction-z)^2)/sum(w), with z=clip(y,-2,2), w=abs(z), zero contribution when total weight <1e-8. Both arms use the same clipped labels, weights and fitting mask; disable optional propensity, class, since, episode, auxiliary, target-shift and importance weights. Verify the canonical objective adapter realizes this contract before admission. The difference includes the declared prediction clipping inside Pearson; it is a loss comparison, not a proof that replay alone causes improvement. Bind model width/depth, input assembly, optimizer, LR/schedule, ordering, gradient clipping, resume/checkpoint details, data paths/hashes and fold memberships from the clean registry before admission. Both arms use strict FP32 for weights, activations, states, gradients and optimizer; autocast/GradScaler off, TF32 off, float32 matmul precision highest.

5. **Thirty paired runs.** Future CP30 matrix: 30 paired fold×seed cells per arm (60 endpoint fits total). F0/F1 use seeds 1001–1008; F2/F3 use seeds 1001–1007. Candidate and control pair on the same cell, source-qualified membership, initialization, row groups, update count, checkpoint rule and scorer. Exact memberships and hashes are currently unbound. These exposed folds are not a new holdout. No fit is authorized by this proposal; a profile or gradient audit does not count as a scientific cell.

6. **Validation and significance.** Keep the official `global_wp_clip2_v1` scorer unchanged: score each target separately on the official evaluation mask `need_prediction AND is_scored`, with prediction/target clipping at ±2 and weights from absolute clipped labels. Training uses fitting-membership labels only under `need_prediction` plus canonical warm-up handling; validation labels and masks never enter fitting. Primary statistic: `D=(1/4) * sum_f mean_s[WP(candidate_f,s)-WP(control_f,s)]`, with equal fold weights and 8/8/7/7 seed pairs. Use the shared continuation protocol: 10,000 paired seed-bootstrap draws with shared seed multiplicities across folds (RNG `20261018`), plus a separate paired component bootstrap on fixed predictions; report the fixed folds and marginal intervals. Apply its two-contrast multiplicity adjustment. These intervals are conditional on the exposed folds and do not cover unseen regimes or public transfer; 30 cells are not 30 IID holdouts.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Inputs remain causal and sequence-local; reset state between sequences. Only training-membership labels on canonical `need_prediction` rows, with existing warm-up semantics, may form the loss. No validation labels/masks, future targets, `is_scored` fit mask, target-derived input/gate, external market data, or cross-sequence cache/state may enter fitting or inference. Fit transforms only on training membership. The official validation mask is used only for endpoint scoring. All CP30 folds are exposed development data; anonymous source/regime coverage limits transfer claims.

8. **Decision-changing result.** The proposed useful-effect gate is `D >= +0.0005`, family-adjusted seed and component interval lower bounds above zero, and measured candidate total training time at most `2x` its matched control. These are not measured results. If all gates pass, consider a separately authorized follow-up on the objective or its student transfer; do not add this delta to any parent score. If the no-fit gradient audit fails, do not fit. If the CP30 gate is uncertain or negative, retain all cells and narrow the conclusion to this fixed macrostep recipe; a zero-crossing interval alone does not reject the wider objective family.

9. **How to run.** From a full checkout at repository root, the documented plan-only command is:

   `python scripts/experiment_draft_plan.py research/experiment_drafts/current-moment-wp-replay/recipe.json`

   It reads the recipe and prints the paired plan; it does not access data, allocate devices, fit, infer, profile, or score. This command was not run. There is no training command because the replay adapter and clean configuration bindings do not exist in this packet. Actual environment, GPU topology/profile, data/cache paths, output directory and resume contract are unbound; add them only after implementation review and separate training authority. Expected plan-only output is JSON on stdout; there is no model output path yet.

10. **Evidence to return.** Before a future fit, freeze source/config/environment/data/membership hashes, clean initialization ancestry, exact optimizer/schedule and paired command. For every cell retain objective and gradient diagnostics, loss, LR, preclip gradient norm, attempted/successful update counts, replay parity, elapsed/load/evaluation time, throughput, peak RAM/VRAM, endpoint predictions and grade manifests, failures/exclusions and fixed checkpoint identity. Preserve separate evidence and weights archives with SHA256 and approved private storage paths.

11. **Results and trace.** Not implemented, profiled, fit, or graded. Measured WP delta and runtime are null; leaderboard/public-transfer effect is unknown. The source-level negative history remains: H-018/E-023 refuted pure per-chunk correlation after degenerate constant-target chunks; H-055/E-291 rejected the tested decay-0.995 pooled-memory recipe, including a two-stage pooled-minus-batch-correlation delta of `-0.001521` with conditional 95% interval `[-0.002868,-0.000161]`. The H-055 ledger's stale `queued` status does not erase E-291. This candidate changes the moments to the current fixed superbatch and replays their gradient; it does not claim to overturn the prior evidence without a new comparison.

## Proposal-specific sources

- Gao et al., [Scaling Deep Contrastive Learning Batch Size under Memory Limited Setup](https://arxiv.org/html/2101.06983v2), sections 3.2–3.3: graphless output pass, loss gradient with respect to cached outputs, and replayed sub-batch backpropagation. Their contrastive-retrieval setting does not establish forecast quality or recurrent-state correctness here.
- Authors' [Gradient Cache implementation](https://github.com/luyug/GradCache/blob/main/src/grad_cache/grad_cache.py): `forward_no_grad`, RNG snapshots via `RandContext`, cached output gradients, and replayed backward (`forward_backward`). Recurrent hidden-state, mask, reset, strict-FP32 and TBPTT parity are still project work.
- Wang, Fang & Liu, [Stochastic Compositional Gradient Descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.3803), abstract only: context for nonlinear functions of expected moments; no finite-batch nonconvex-GRU or official-score guarantee is transferred.

See also the [shared literature review](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/current-moment-wp-replay/research/unified/sources/GRADIENT_ESTIMATOR_LITERATURE_20261018.md), [shared continuation and CP30 protocol](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/current-moment-wp-replay/research/unified/ideas/GRADIENT_ESTIMATOR_CONTINUATIONS_20261018.md), and [H-055/H-018 reframe](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/current-moment-wp-replay/research/unified/ideas/EVENT_STATE_AND_METRIC_OBJECTIVE_REFRAME_20261015_R1.md).
